english: Let $y:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function such that $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=y-x^{2}$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}\dfrac{y(x)}{x^{3}}$ exists as a real number. Then the value of $y(6)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $y:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ एक अवकलनीय फलन है जिसके लिए सभी $x\in\mathbb{R}$ हेतु $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=y-x^{2}$ है तथा $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}\dfrac{y(x)}{x^{3}}$ एक वास्तविक संख्या के रूप में विद्यमान है। तब $y(6)$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Condition at infinity: $\dfrac{e^{x}}{x^{3}}\to\infty$, so the limit is finite only if $C=0$
solution_full: Write the equation as $y'-y=-x^{2}$, linear with $P=-1$; integrating factor $e^{-x}$.
So $y=x^{2}+2x+2+Ce^{x}$. Every real $C$ gives a solution on $\mathbb{R}$; a condition is needed to fix $C$. Here it is a boundary condition at infinity.

$\dfrac{y}{x^{3}}=\dfrac{x^{2}+2x+2}{x^{3}}+C\dfrac{e^{x}}{x^{3}}$. The first part tends to $0$; $\dfrac{e^{x}}{x^{3}}\to\infty$. So the limit is a real number only when $C=0$ (it is $+\infty$ for $C>0$ and $-\infty$ for $C<0$).
originality_note: New: a linear equation whose solution is selected by a growth condition at infinity instead of an initial value; only the polynomial solution survives (way 5). Closest known: y' - y = -x^2 with y(0) given. Different because: the student must see that the e^x term destroys the limit, so C = 0.
blueprint_concepts: Initial value and boundary value problems
Linear differential equation in y; integrating factor

concept_use.Initial value and boundary value problem: The constant of the general solution is fixed not by an initial value but by the growth condition at infinity (a boundary condition), which selects the polynomial solution.
concept_use.Linear differential equation in y; integ: The equation y' - y = -x^2 is linear with integrating factor e^{-x}, solved by integrating by parts twice.

key_step: General solution x^2 + 2x + 2 + Ce^x; the limit forces C = 0.
